types.oie_definition: An organization engaged in commercial, industrial, or professional activities.
types.embedding_query_text: Company: An organization engaged in commercial, industrial, or professional activities. Also called Business, Corporation, Enterprise, Firm, Organization.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are specific corporations, aligning with the definition and examples in Corporation.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.oie_definition: A numerical measure of positions eliminated or affected in an employment context.
types.embedding_query_text: Job Count: A numerical measure of positions eliminated or affected in an employment context. Also called Workforce Reduction, Staffing Change, Employment Adjustment, Personnel Count, Workforce Metric.

chosen_type.label: JobCount
chosen_type.definition: A numerical measure of employment positions affected or eliminated.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate captures the specific employment context of the mentions.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: EmployerAggregateRating
candidates.comment: An EmployerAggregateRating is an AggregateRating representing a collective assessment of an Organization's performance as an employer. Also called company rating, employer review score, workplace satisfaction rating. Examples: Glassdoor's overall rating for a company, an average employee satisfaction score, a composite rating from multiple employee surveys.

types.oie_definition: A specialized business unit focused on developing or managing a specific product or service.
types.embedding_query_text: Product Division: A specialized business unit focused on developing or managing a specific product or service. Also called Business Unit, Division, Product Line, Corporate Division, Subsidiary Unit.

chosen_type.label: ProductGroup
chosen_type.justification: Xbox represents a product line, which aligns with ProductGroup's definition of a variant group.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

types.oie_definition: An individual human being with a distinct identity.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being with a distinct identity. Also called Individual, Human, Individual Person, Personality, Individual Identity.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are distinct human individuals, matching the Person type.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.oie_definition: A specific role or rank within an organization or hierarchy.
types.embedding_query_text: Position: A specific role or rank within an organization or hierarchy. Also called Role, Job Title, Post, Rank, Designation.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: The mentions describe specific corporate roles, fitting OrganizationRole's definition.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

types.oie_definition: A specific point in time marked by day, month, and year.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time marked by day, month, and year. Also called Calendar Date, Temporal Point, Day, Specific Date, Chronological Marker.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The first mention is a valid ISO 8601 date. 'Next year' is a relative time and not a valid Date instance.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.oie_definition: A period of 365 days as a unit of time measurement.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 days as a unit of time measurement. Also called Calendar Year, Annual Period, 12-Month Cycle, Time Period, Annual Unit.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Years are periods of time, aligning with Duration's definition of time spans.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.oie_definition: An online service enabling user-generated content and public communication.
types.embedding_query_text: Social Media Platform: An online service enabling user-generated content and public communication. Also called Online Network, Digital Platform, Social Network, Messaging Service, Public Forum.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online service enabling user-generated content and public communication.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a social media platform as a distinct entity.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: UserComments
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of posting comments or feedback. Also called user comment, public comment, feedback post. Examples: a user leaving a comment on a blog post, posting a review, providing feedback on a product.

types.oie_definition: A business model providing ongoing access to content or services for a recurring fee.
types.embedding_query_text: Subscription Service: A business model providing ongoing access to content or services for a recurring fee. Also called Recurring Access, Membership Service, Ongoing Service, Access Model, Subscription Plan.

chosen_type.label: SubscriptionService
chosen_type.definition: A service providing ongoing access to content or resources for a recurring fee.
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'Game Pass' implies a recurring access model not captured by existing schema.org candidates.

candidates.label: SubscribeAction
candidates.comment: The act of forming a unidirectional connection to receive continuous updates from an object or entity. Also called subscribing, following for updates, signing up for notifications. Examples: subscribing to a YouTube channel, signing up for a newsletter, subscribing to a podcast. Distinct from FollowAction, which implies a more reciprocal or social connection. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is a one-time enrollment.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: PaymentService
candidates.comment: A PaymentService, as a FinancialProduct, is a service to transfer funds between persons or organizations. Also called money transfer service, payment processing service, remittance service. Examples: PayPal, Western Union, a bank's wire transfer service. Distinct from BankAccount, which is an account, not a service.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

types.oie_definition: A series of video games sharing a common theme or brand identity.
types.embedding_query_text: Video Game Franchise: A series of video games sharing a common theme or brand identity. Also called Game Series, Franchise Brand, Entertainment Series, Interactive Media Series, Game Collection.

chosen_type.label: VideoGameSeries
chosen_type.justification: Call of Duty is a well-known video game series, matching VideoGameSeries' definition.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

types.oie_definition: A field of knowledge involving the application of scientific principles to practical tasks.
types.embedding_query_text: Technology: A field of knowledge involving the application of scientific principles to practical tasks. Also called Technical Field, Scientific Application, Innovation Domain, Engineering Discipline, Technical Innovation.

chosen_type.label: Technology
chosen_type.definition: A field of knowledge involving the application of scientific principles to practical tasks.
chosen_type.justification: AI is a technology field not directly mapped to existing schema.org candidates like SoftwareApplication.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.

types.oie_definition: The official name of a specific video game product.
types.embedding_query_text: Video Game Title: The official name of a specific video game product. Also called Game Name, Interactive Work Title, Digital Entertainment Title, Entertainment Product Name, Game Product Name.

chosen_type.label: VideoGame
chosen_type.justification: Both mentions are specific video game titles, aligning with VideoGame's definition.

candidates.label: VideoGame
candidates.comment: An electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device. Also called computer game, console game, digital game. Examples: Super Mario Bros., The Legend of Zelda, Call of Duty.

candidates.label: VideoGameClip
candidates.comment: A short segment or part of a video game, often used for promotional or highlight purposes. Also called game clip, gameplay footage, video game segment. Examples: a highlight reel from an e-sports match, a trailer showing a game's cutscene, a short recording of a player's achievement.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.
